title: I Built an AI Agent in 5 Minutes (And Sold It Live)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Chris promotes AI voice agents and points viewers toward his group's free lead-scraping service; he names tools he prefers, but no paid sponsorship is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: How do you even watch Netflix with your wife and ignore your phone when you could have a $3,000 job on the end of the line?
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: AI voice-agent installation for small businesses
idea.one_liner: Build and install AI phone agents for small businesses that miss calls, charging a monthly fee.
idea.customer: Small businesses, especially service businesses that take calls while working in the field.
idea.offer: An AI voice agent that answers inbound calls, handles common questions, gathers caller details, and can pass inquiries to the business.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly service fee; the speaker says businesses may pay $500 to $2,000 per month.

key_quotes.quote: This is one that business owners are actually paying for today, and that's AI voice agents.
So, the hard part here is finding the customers, finding who to actually pay you $500 to $2,000 a month for these AI voice agents that you can build in 5 minutes.
So, if you have a tree trimming business in the state of Texas, I can install an AI voice agent for you and it will not cost nearly as much as you think.

claims.claim: The speaker says businesses may pay $500 to $2,000 per month for voice agents.
claims.quote: So, the hard part here is finding the customers, finding who to actually pay you $500 to $2,000 a month for these AI voice agents that you can build in 5 minutes.

claims.claim: He says drag-and-drop tools can build an agent in five minutes or less.
claims.quote: They're really realistic, and you can use drag and drop easy tools to build them in 5 minutes or less.

claims.claim: He planned to send ringless voicemails to 500 business owners in the live campaign.
claims.quote: I'm going to show you my phone, my Google Voice account, and I'm going to send ringless voicemail drops to 500 business owners, wait for them to call me back, and try to close a deal for an AI voice agent.

claims.claim: In his experience, one third to one half of scraped numbers are valid cell numbers.
claims.quote: And in my experience, usually a third to half of your scraped numbers will be like valid cell phone numbers.

claims.claim: He says scraping leads yourself costs about $4 and may take 24 or 72 hours over a weekend.
claims.quote: It costs like $4 to scrape these leads. So, if you don't want to wait however long it takes us to get them, which could be 24 or 72 hours if it's over the weekend, then you can do it yourself.

claims.claim: He estimates people may give a voicemail two to five seconds, and 10% may listen to a ten-second message.
claims.quote: Fact of the matter is I probably have like for most people I probably have two seconds. For most other people I probably have five and maybe 10% of people will listen to a 10-second voicemail.

claims.claim: The pitch frames a missed call as risking a $3,000 tree-trimming job.
claims.quote: How do you even watch Netflix with your wife and ignore your phone when you could have a $3,000 job on the end of the line?

claims.claim: He uploaded 475 numbers, estimating that 25 of 500 were invalid.
claims.quote: Upload 475 numbers. Why 475 instead of 500? Because 25 were probably invalid.

claims.claim: He estimates callbacks will be in the mid-to-low single digits, with many callers not having heard the voicemail.
claims.quote: I'm going to say for call back, it's probably going to be mid to low single digits for people that call back. Now, a lot, maybe even most of the call backs will be people that did not hear the voicemail.

claims.claim: He estimates 1% to 8% of the numbers will call back.
claims.quote: I would say like I don't know 1 to 8% of these numbers will will

claims.claim: He estimates that 20% to 60% of callbacks will have heard the voicemail.
claims.quote: of those maybe 20 to 60% will actually have heard the voicemail and therefore probably have some level of interest

claims.claim: At one point in the campaign, 86 drops had been reported successful.
claims.quote: Then you can look at the stats down here. So 86 have been successful.

claims.claim: Later, 177 drops had been reported successful.
claims.quote: So, 177 have been successful so far. I got another guy that said stop.

claims.claim: The final shown campaign count was 282 successful out of a 500-number campaign, reported as 56%.
claims.quote: So these have all sent. I just did a control find for pending 00 successful 282. So 56% of these were successful.

acquisition_channels.details: The demonstrated campaign sent ringless voicemail drops to scraped business phone numbers and waited for callbacks.
He recommends manually answering callbacks and describes calling prospects back; UK cold calls need TPS/CTPS screening.
He suggests text as a possible follow-up in a multi-touch campaign.
He lists email as a possible touch in a multi-channel campaign.
He lists LinkedIn outreach as a possible touch.
He says agents can be sold through the GoHighLevel app marketplace.

ideas.delivery: The operator builds and configures an inbound voice agent in GoHighLevel, loads business FAQs or website content as its knowledge base, connects or ports a phone number, and sends call details to the business for follow-up.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The suggested outreach mix includes cold texts to business-owner numbers, which is prohibited when sent to UK individuals or sole traders. Cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS; the ringless-voicemail approach also needs UK PECR review before use.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to scraped lead data, including lawful basis, transparency, and suppression. Cold email is permitted only to limited companies with an opt-out. Monthly subscriptions should account for DMCC Act requirements.
